title: The Arrogant Watermelon
summary: The watermelon thinks it is the biggest and the best. But one day it needs help from its small friends.
moral: A big body does not make someone more noble. Be humble, for we all need one another.
pages: At the edge of the garden lived a big, round Watermelon. 'I am the biggest and sweetest fruit here!' it said every day, puffing out its chest.
'You are so small,' Watermelon mocked Strawberry and Grape. 'You are useless. Only I can make people full!' Strawberry and Grape lowered their heads sadly, but they stayed polite.
One morning Watermelon rolled along the path singing. 'See how fast I am!' Too carried away, it did not see a big hole in front of it.
Thud! Watermelon fell into the hole. Its big, round body was too slippery to climb out. 'Help! Help me!' it cried in panic. But no one heard.
Strawberry and Grape heard the cries. Even though they had been mocked, they did not think twice. 'Let us help Watermelon!' They ran as fast as they could to the edge of the hole.
Their bodies were too small to pull Watermelon out. So they called Elephant, who was passing by. With his strong trunk, Elephant lifted Watermelon out of the hole carefully.

'Thank you, Strawberry and Grape, and Elephant,' said Watermelon, ashamed. 'Forgive me for being arrogant. It turns out I need your help too.' They laughed happily, and from then on Watermelon became a humble fruit. The end.
